You are analyzing the git repository at /home/user/fortress (a revival of Sun/Oracle's Fortress language; full 2007-2012 history). Read /home/user/fortress/CLAUDE.md first for project context.

The remote (origin) has these branches besides `main` and `claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr`: John, john, ange_michael, bird_count, hygiene, node-interface, perftesting, syntax, syntax2, syntax3, syntax4, works. These came with the 2016 GitHub fork of the historical repo (originally Mercurial, converted to git). `main` currently contains the 2012 trunk HEAD a874948 plus 2026 revival commits.

Task: for EACH of those branches, determine (fetch them if not present locally: `git fetch origin <branch>`):
1. Its tip commit (sha, date, author) and the merge-base with a874948 (the 2012 trunk head).
2. How many commits it has that are NOT in main (`git log --oneline origin/<branch> ^main | wc -l`), and whether it has ANY unique content at all — some may be fully merged into trunk already (`git log main --oneline | head` comparison, or ahead/behind counts via `git rev-list --left-right --count`).
3. If it has unique commits: who wrote them, when (date range), and what they are about — read the commit messages and skim representative diffs (`git log --stat` on a few). Identify the theme (e.g. syntax-abstraction work, performance experiments, bird-count demo work, hygiene = macro hygiene?, node-interface = AST work?).
4. Whether the unique work was later superseded/re-landed on trunk in different commits (check if similar file changes exist in main's history).

Then produce a report: a table (branch | tip date | author(s) | commits not in main | theme | recommendation) followed by a short per-branch paragraph. Recommendations must be conservative, from: KEEP (unique historical content, part of the preserved artifact), MERGE (content that would benefit main — unlikely for 2012 research branches, justify carefully), or DELETE (strictly zero unique commits, i.e. fully contained in main — nothing lost by deletion). When in doubt, KEEP: this repo's purpose is historical preservation. Note that branch deletion loses the branch NAME even when commits are contained; mention tagging (e.g. `archive/<branch>`) as an alternative if relevant.

Do NOT modify the repository — read-only analysis (fetching branches is fine). Return the full report as your final message.

All data gathered. One clarifying detail on the local repo: it was a shallow clone (74 commits), so I ran `git fetch --unshallow` to get the full 5,397-commit history before computing merge-bases — read-only otherwise.

# Report: Historical branches on origin (palimondo/fortress)

All twelve branches are relics of the Sun-era Mercurial/SVN repository, carried over by the 2016 GitHub conversion. A key pattern: every branch that was "finished" ends in an **empty hg close-branch commit** (David Chase's 2012-01-20 "closing X, tired of it" sweep), and the 2008-era research branches were re-landed on trunk via **svn-merge commits that squash the branch history** — so the branch heads are the *only* record of the fine-grained, per-author development steps, even where the final content is fully in trunk.

## Summary table

| Branch | Tip (sha, date) | Author(s) of unique commits | Not in main | Theme | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| John | c111201cb, 2011-12-07 | — (tip by Jean-Baptiste Tristan, in main) | **0** | stale pointer into trunk history | DELETE (or tag `archive/John`) |
| john | abc8f4807, 2012-01-27 | Tristan King | 1 (empty) | hg branch-open marker only (linker work stayed on trunk) | KEEP (or tag+delete) |
| ange_michael | 259a02d3a, 2012-01-20 | angelee, mspiegel | 35 (34 real) | bytecode top-level environment generation, Jun 2008 | KEEP |
| bird_count | 074f85872, 2012-05-25 | — (tip by David Chase, in main) | **0** | stale pointer into trunk history | DELETE (or tag `archive/bird_count`) |
| hygiene | f506b7d8b, 2012-01-20 | jon | 6 (5 real) | macro hygiene: alpha-renaming, syntax environments, Sep 2008 | KEEP |
| node-interface | 6908e4fe2, 2012-01-20 | jon | 4 (3 real) | astgen-generated syntax-abstraction AST nodes, Feb–Mar 2009 — **never landed** | KEEP |
| perftesting | dbcdf92aa, 2012-01-20 | mspiegel | 13 (12 real) | performance-test monitor + JFreeChart graphing, Aug 2008; orphan root, later work never landed | KEEP |
| syntax | e2c818a34, 2012-01-20 | jon, ryanc | 39 (38 real) | syntax abstraction round 1: pattern variables, non-terminal typing | KEEP |
| syntax2 | 63135681e, 2012-01-20 | jon, ryanc | 29 (28 real) | syntax abstraction round 2: template parser, 2-stage macro expansion | KEEP |
| syntax3 | 7159d9f7f, 2012-01-20 | jon, ryanc | 21 (20 real) | syntax abstraction round 3: `=>` transformers, case macros, super-syntax | KEEP |
| syntax4 | 9571c665d, 2012-01-20 | jon | 10 (9 real) | syntax abstraction round 4: ellipses (`...`) in macro templates | KEEP |
| works | 0f5f3f3d2, 2012-01-25 | David Chase | 3 (2 merges + 1 empty) | Jan 2012 compiler merge staging; tree identical to main's a2b230d0b | KEEP (or tag+delete) |

Merge-bases with a874948 (2012 trunk head): John = its own tip; john = 4b0f942fb (2012-01-27); ange_michael = cb83d6fc0 (2008-06-05); bird_count = its own tip; hygiene = 2f59dbebd (2008-09-19); node-interface = f1b358d34 (2009-02-22); perftesting = **none** (disconnected orphan root ad808cfa6, 2008-08-05); syntax = 3eab1e730 (2008-05-30); syntax2 = fca589bbb (2008-07-15); syntax3 = 1fbf3dcd6 (2008-08-01); syntax4 = 2f5a95733 (2008-08-06); works = 22c12feb7 (2012-01-25).

## Per-branch notes

**John** — Points at c111201cb (Jean-Baptiste Tristan, 2011-12-07, in the middle of trunk history). `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms full containment; zero unique commits. Nothing but the name is lost by deletion. The capital-J/lowercase-j pair is almost certainly an hg branch-naming artifact of the git conversion. Safe DELETE; `git tag archive/John c111201cb` preserves where the hg branch pointed if you want the label kept.

**john** — One unique commit, abc8f4807 "Starting 'john' branch" (Tristan King, 2012-01-27), which is **empty** (an hg branch-open marker; its parent 4b0f942fb "some code to plug the linker on top of the repository" is on trunk). Zero content, but strictly not zero commits, so under your conservative rule: KEEP, or tag `archive/john` and delete.

**ange_michael** — Angelee (Kim) + Michael Spiegel (hence the name), 2008-06-10 to 2008-06-18: the first compiled top-level environments — `TopLevelEnvGenerator.java` emitting a `<Component>Environment.class` per component via ASM, binary-search get/put in bytecode, the project's first JUnit test for it. **Superseded on trunk**: c15629abf (mspiegel, 2008-06-18) "Merging [compiler] branch r2001 into the main trunk" squash-landed it; the code lives on in main as `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/environments/TopLevelEnvGen.java`. The branch preserves the only per-commit record of who wrote what. KEEP.

**bird_count** — Tip 074f85872 (David Chase, 2012-05-25) is fully contained in main — the hg "bird count" demo branch (a62b3f3a4 "Starting 'bird count' branch") was merged back to trunk, marker commit and all. Zero unique commits. Safe DELETE; tag `archive/bird_count` if the name is worth keeping (it marks where the Birds demo work happened, and Sample/birds material is in trunk).

**hygiene** — Jon Rafkind, 2008-09-20 to 09-22: real macro hygiene — `SyntaxEnvironment.java`, fresh-name generation for local var decls, alpha-renaming moved to VarRef, template-gap lookup in the syntax environment, hygiene restricted to macro calls. **Superseded**: trunk commit fd30f0b14 (jon, 2008-09-22) "[merge] svn merge -r2850:HEAD .../branches/hygiene", and `SyntaxEnvironment.java` exists in main today. The five development commits exist only here. KEEP.

**node-interface** — Jon Rafkind, Feb–Mar 2009: making the syntax-abstraction AST nodes (template gaps, ellipses, transformations) generated by astgen instead of hand-hacked — adds `astgen/SyntaxAbstractionCreator.java` (154 lines) and `astgen/README-interface`. **Never landed**: neither file exists anywhere in main's history, and there is no node-interface merge commit. This is genuinely unique, unmerged work — the strongest KEEP of the set.

**perftesting** — Michael Spiegel, Aug 2008. Unusual topology: a disconnected **orphan root** ("includes only the source files until the libraries can be OKed by the lawyers" — the JFreeChart jars were the legal problem), so it has *no merge-base with trunk at all*. Trunk got the initial two files separately (42affb1fd, 2008-07-31, `PerformanceLogMonitor.java` + `TestSuiteData.java`), but the branch's subsequent three weeks of work — `ChartWriter.java`, per-chart imagemap HTML, Niagara-friendly threading, y-axis/date-range chart refinements — **never reached trunk** (no `ChartWriter` anywhere in main). KEEP.

**syntax / syntax2 / syntax3 / syntax4** — The core syntax-abstraction (Fortress macros) research line, Jon Rafkind ("jon") and Ryan Culpepper ("ryanc"), May–Aug 2008. Four successive iterations: (1) pattern-variable binding and typing of non-terminals; (2) the template parser, `_SyntaxTransformation` nodes, and two-stage macro expansion ("stage 2 of the core calculus"); (3) the `=>` pattern/template separator, case transformers, super-syntax, graceful lookup errors; (4) ellipses (`...`) lists in templates, the regex and XML macro examples, `fortress_`-prefixed Rats! variables. Each was svn-merged into trunk immediately after its last commit — 4295ddf2f (r1752:1883, Jun 12), 99ae14ddc (Jul 31), cbae53bb6 (syntax3, Aug 6), f2dce1624 (syntax4, Aug 8) — and trunk then evolved the ideas further (e.g. 2b144d309 eliminating syntax4's EllipsesEnvironment). The squash merges mean these ~95 fine-grained commits, including all of Culpepper's individual authorship, exist **only** on these branches. KEEP all four.

**works** — David Chase, 2012-01-25: two merge commits ("More merges", "yam") staging the type-checker/codegen merge work of that week, plus the empty "Closing this branch no longer needed". The resolved tree of ca9014495 is byte-identical to main's a2b230d0b ("yet another merge to placate our stupid tools"), and `git cherry` finds no unique patches — content fully in main; only the merge topology is unique. KEEP under the conservative rule, or tag `archive/works` and delete.

## Overall recommendation

Keep everything except, at most, **John** and **bird_count**, the only two with strictly zero unique commits — and even for those, prefer `git tag archive/<branch> <tip>` before deletion, since the branch *names* themselves are historical metadata (they record which hg named branches existed at Oracle). For a preservation-focused repo, tagging all twelve as `archive/*` and leaving the branches in place costs nothing. No branch contains anything that should be merged into main: all mergeable content already landed on the 2008–2012 trunk in superseding commits, and the never-landed remnants (node-interface's astgen creator, perftesting's chart tooling) are 2008/2009-era experiments of archival, not practical, value.

No local changes were made to the working tree or refs beyond fetching the remote branches and unshallowing history.
